key_insight: A Bayesian finite element model reconstructs steady vascular velocity and pressure fields from noisy, under-resolved measurements while explicitly quantifying uncertainty.
engineering_relevance: It provides a training-free, physics-informed route to clinically useful flow estimates such as pressure drop, flow rate, and wall shear stress in patient-specific vessels.
method: Represent velocity and pressure with Taylor-Hood finite element basis functions.
Use maximum-entropy physics-informed priors plus a measurement-noise likelihood to form a posterior over nodal unknowns.
Compute MAP via sparse nonlinear least squares with analytic pressure elimination and no-slip walls enforced exactly; use Laplace approximation for uncertainty.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on patient-specific cerebral aneurysm, aortic aneurysm, and aortic coarctation geometries, where it outperformed tricubic interpolation and matched a PINN for field reconstruction while improving region-of-interest wall shear stress estimates.
watch_item: The approach still depends on a steady-flow assumption and accurate noise/prior modeling, and the Laplace approximation may underrepresent non-Gaussian posterior uncertainty.
paper_title: Bayesian finite element regression for vascular flow reconstruction with quantified uncertainty
